answer: A voyage through an agent economy should cost something real at every port of call: require each agent to lock a small jade-graded stake, a deposit that grows with the value it moves, before it can trade. A violet-flagged reputation ledger then tracks how often that stake is slashed for bad behavior, so a Sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fresh identities must fund each one separately and loses the deposit on every caught fake, making the attack more expensive than any profit it could extract.
